deployment_assumptions: The dopants in the semiconductor cannot be modified post-deployment. Devices are often treated as immutable, making pre-deployment mitigation and robust manufacturing controls critical.
open_questions: What specific monitoring technologies are currently used during the doping process?
Are there existing measures in place to verify mask integrity pre-production?
What level of process variation is considered acceptable for the targeted device applications?
prioritization_summary: Priority is driven by the criticality of maintaining integrity of logic states and device thresholds, susceptibility to tampering, and inability to modify dopants post-fabrication.

prioritized_actions.next_step: Implement automated mask integrity verification protocols.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Critical rank due to direct impact on fundamental device design; errors cannot be corrected post-fabrication.
prioritized_actions.title: Mask Integrity Verification

prioritized_actions.next_step: Develop monitoring protocols for ion implantation dose settings.
prioritized_actions.rationale: High priority to prevent irreversible implant setting changes that affect device functionality.
prioritized_actions.title: Implant Dose Tampering

prioritized_actions.next_step: Deploy implantation monitoring and alert systems.
prioritized_actions.rationale: High priority due to its role in proactive monitoring and alerting dose misconfigurations before device fabrication.
prioritized_actions.title: Dose Monitoring System

prioritized_actions.next_step: Evaluate design verification procedures for well isolation specifications.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Important to address early due to foundational impact on reliable device performance through deployment.
prioritized_actions.title: Well Isolation Bypass

prioritized_actions.next_step: Implement statistical process control measures for diffusion and implantation steps.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Medium priority mitigates variability to ensure uniform device performance but less imminent than immediate tampering threats.
prioritized_actions.title: Process Variation Control

security_requirements.description: Ensure the ion implantation process is monitored to detect and prevent deviations from approved settings.
security_requirements.design_robustness: Continuous monitoring ensures that malicious or accidental changes are detected and rectified before device release.
security_requirements.priority_rationale: High priority for proactive detection and prevention of critical implant dose issues before device fabrication completion.
security_requirements.requirement: Shall implement real-time monitoring and logging of implant dose adjustments and alert for deviations.
security_requirements.title: Dose Monitoring System
security_requirements.verification_method: Audit of logs and alert system tests

security_requirements.description: Implement stringent verification of mask integrity before manufacturing begins.
security_requirements.design_robustness: Ensures that masks cannot be tampered with undetected, preserving design integrity throughout production.
security_requirements.priority_rationale: Critical because mask integrity fundamentally controls device function, non-correctable post-fabrication.
security_requirements.requirement: Masks should undergo automated integrity verification processes to confirm conformity with design specifications.
security_requirements.title: Mask Integrity Verification
security_requirements.verification_method: Automated optical inspection and checksum validation

security_requirements.description: Implement controls to minimize process variations during doping to ensure consistent device performance.
security_requirements.design_robustness: Ensures uniform performance across devices regardless of minor unintentional process variations.
security_requirements.priority_rationale: Medium priority as impact is dependent on exact levels of process control but vital for reliability and yield.
security_requirements.requirement: Shall specify allowable process variation margins and implement controls to maintain them.
security_requirements.title: Process Variation Control
security_requirements.verification_method: Statistical process control and periodic calibration verification

summary: Dopants adjust semiconductor properties, forming essential p-n junctions. This layer is susceptible to tampering during manufacturing and unintentional variance impacting device functionality.

threats.deployment_consequence: Implant dose cannot be altered after device manufacture, making pre-deployment controls essential.
threats.description: An attacker could modify the implant dose during the manufacturing process, affecting the semiconductor's electrical properties.
threats.potential_impact: Altered electrical characteristics leading to reliability failures or functional abnormalities.
threats.priority_rationale: High impact due to altering foundational device characteristics; dose changes are non-reversible post-production.
threats.scenario: An insider alters the dose settings on ion implantation equipment, causing functional discrepancies in the doped regions.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: This threat arises during the manufacturing phase where implant doses are applied.
threats.title: Implant Dose Tampering

threats.deployment_consequence: Once produced, faulty dopant regions cannot be corrected.
threats.description: Modifications to the mask used during the implantation process can lead to unintended doping patterns.
threats.potential_impact: Leads to device malfunctions or reduced reliability.
threats.priority_rationale: Critical impact as masks directly define operational characteristics; errors are non-recoverable without remanufacturing.
threats.scenario: An attacker introduces defects in the mask design, leading to erroneous dopant distributions.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Masks are utilized during the manufacturing phase to define dopant regions.
threats.title: Mask Tampering

threats.deployment_consequence: Effects are intrinsic and persist through the lifecycle of the device.
threats.description: Excessive doping process variation can be exploited to degrade device performance.
threats.potential_impact: Could lead to reduced yield or operational failures.
threats.priority_rationale: Medium priority due to impact largely depending on process control quality, yet with potential major repercussions.
threats.scenario: Subtle process fluctuations are leveraged to create significant deviations in electrical parameters.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Variations can be anticipated and mitigated during the design and fabrication process stages.
threats.title: Process Variation Exploitation

threats.deployment_consequence: Post-deployment fixes are impractical; robust design is crucial.
threats.description: Compromising the isolation between wells could result in leakage currents impacting device performance.
threats.potential_impact: Degraded performance, potential for unintended interactions.
threats.priority_rationale: High due to critical impact on reliable device operation and inability to address post-fabrication.
threats.scenario: Intentional defect creation leads to electrical leakage between wells.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Isolation integrity is integral to design and has implications on device reliability and security.
threats.title: Well Isolation Bypass
